<h2 class="wp-block-heading" id="why-i-love-this">Creamy Lemon Sauce On Salmon = SO GOOD</h2>


<div class="wp-block-image lindsay-headshot is-style-rounded">
<figure class="alignright size-large is-resized"><img width="1600" height="1600" decoding="async" data-pin-url="https://pinchofyum.com/baked-salmon-with-amazing-lemon-sauce?tp_image_id=94266" data-pin-description="Baked Salmon with Amazing Lemon Sauce! Delicious baked salmon with crispy potatoes, broccoli, and the most amazing life-changing lemon sauce smothered on top of it all. This is restaurant bistro-style eating! #salmon #lemonsauce #sheetpan" data-pin-title="Baked Salmon with Amazing Lemon Sauce" data-pin-nopin="nopin" loading="eager" src="https://pinchofyum.com/tachyon/Lindsay-Post-Notes-960x960.jpg" alt="Lindsay Ostrom headshot. " class="wp-image-94266" style="width:222px;height:undefinedpx" srcset="https://pinchofyum.com/tachyon/Lindsay-Post-Notes-960x960.jpg?resize=1600%2C1600&zoom=1 1600w, https://pinchofyum.com/tachyon/Lindsay-Post-Notes-960x960.jpg?resize=1600%2C1600&zoom=0.5 800w, https://pinchofyum.com/tachyon/Lindsay-Post-Notes-960x960.jpg?resize=1600%2C1600&zoom=0.25 400w" sizes="(max-width: 1600px) 100vw, 1600px"></figure>
</div>


<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Crispy golden brown roasted potatoes: HELLO yes.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Tender baby broccoli with a little crunchy char: check check. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Baked salmon, simply salted, peppered, brushed with olive oil, and baked to flaky perfection: absolutely.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">And enter -> the herby, creamy, lemony lemon sauce. Yes, yes, and y-e-s. Everything else is delicious, but if we’re being honest, it really just serves in the supporting role for this sauce. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">This lemon sauce is a showstopper. It’s creamy and rich and light all at the same time. It starts with shallots and gets infused with a few sprigs of fresh thyme and finished with a little sizzle of lemon juice, and it feels like there should be more to explain but really, that is the beauty of it. It’s simple and it’s got really beautiful, gentle, universally delicious flavor and just MWAH.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">This is me raising my glass to you as we eat salmon smothered in lemon sauce with bites of crispy potato and broccoli in our home kitchens / pretend fancy restaurants together. It’s just such a treat and I hope you love it. Enjoy!</p>

<h2 class="wp-block-heading" id="h-why-this-is-the-best-beginner-salmon-recipe">Why This Is The Best Beginner Salmon Recipe</h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Even if you’ve never made salmon before, YOU CAN MAKE this baked salmon for dinner. I know you can.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Baking salmon, to me, feels like the best intro into cooking salmon. It’s simple and hands-off, and all you need to do is check the temperature at the end of the cook time to make sure it’s good to go, and you’ve got salmon for dinner.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">If you’re looking to take it a step further and try cooking it in different ways, check out our how-to guide for <a href="https://pinchofyum.com/how-to-cook-salmon">how to cook salmon</a>.</p>

<li id="instruction-step-1"><strong>Roast the Potatoes:</strong> Preheat the oven to 400 degrees. Line a baking sheet with parchment. Add the potatoes to the pan and toss with olive oil, garlic powder, and salt. Roast for 25 minutes until lightly browned and delicious.<br>
<div class="tasty-recipe-responsive-iframe-container" style="aspect-ratio: 16 / 9;"><iframe loading="lazy" class="fitvidsignore" title="Baked Salmon with Amazing Lemon Sauce Step 1" src="https://player.vimeo.com/video/567549026?dnt=1&app_id=122963&autoplay=0&muted=1&autopause=0&loop=1&controls=1" frameborder="0" allow="autoplay; fullscreen; picture-in-picture; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin"></iframe></div></li>
<li id="instruction-step-2"><strong>Make the Lemon Cream Sauce:</strong> While the potatoes are roasting, make your sauce. Melt the butter over medium low heat. Add the garlic and shallot; sauté for 3-5 minutes until soft and fragrant. Add broth, cream, and thyme; bring to a low simmer. Let the sauce hang out over low heat until it starts to thicken. It will reduce by about half. Remove the thyme sprigs. Whisk in the lemon juice and zest. Give it a taste. Yes, you’re in heaven now.<br>
<div class="tasty-recipe-responsive-iframe-container" style="aspect-ratio: 16 / 9;"><iframe loading="lazy" class="fitvidsignore" title="Baked Salmon with Amazing Lemon Sauce Step 2" src="https://player.vimeo.com/video/567550155?dnt=1&app_id=122963&autoplay=0&muted=1&autopause=0&loop=1&controls=1" frameborder="0" allow="autoplay; fullscreen; picture-in-picture; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin"></iframe></div></li>
<li id="instruction-step-3"><strong>Bake the Salmon and Broccoli:</strong> Add the broccoli and the salmon to the potato pan (keeping the potatoes on there). Toss or brush with a little more olive oil, garlic powder, and salt. <h2 class="faq-heading">Baked Salmon with Amazing Lemon Sauce: FAQs</h2>



<div class="schema-faq wp-block-yoast-faq-block"><div class="schema-faq-section" id="faq-question-1624885400568"><strong class="schema-faq-question">I’m new to making salmon. Do I eat the skin?</strong> <p class="schema-faq-answer">Salmon skin is technically edible, but I personally don’t eat it. I like to just slide the skins off the filets before plating it, since they come off very easily after baking.</p> </div> <div class="schema-faq-section" id="faq-question-1624885291924"><strong class="schema-faq-question">How do I prevent sad, dry salmon?</strong> <p class="schema-faq-answer">Overcooking your salmon will cause it to dry out! And, sad news: it doesn’t taste good. You can use a meat thermometer if you want to get very precise with your temperature – but I usually don’t use one and I just go off of how it looks and feels. I’ll often flake apart one piece to check for a moist, opaque center before deciding if it’s done or if it needs another minute or two in the oven, even though it messes up the presentation slightly. I find that regardless of size of filets or oven variations, somewhere between 10-15 minutes is usually the right amount of time for the doneness that I like.</p> </div> <div class="schema-faq-section" id="faq-question-1624885439437"><strong class="schema-faq-question">I have some extra sauce. Can I save it as leftovers?</strong> <p class="schema-faq-answer">The sauce might thicken and/or separate as you let it rest, so I think it is best served fresh; however, it is still delicious the next day if you just reheat and whisk it back together, maybe adding a little water as needed. Works great on leftover potatoes with an egg for breakfast!</p> </div> <div class="schema-faq-section" id="faq-question-1778094676923"><strong class="schema-faq-question">Can I use half-and-half instead of heavy cream?</strong> <p class="schema-faq-answer">To get the right thickness and texture, I highly recommend using heavy whipping cream for this recipe. If you only have half-and-half, you could also add a small amount of cornstarch slurry at the end to thicken things up.</p> </div> </div>

				<meta itemprop="name" content="marie">
				<cite class="fn">marie</cite>			</div>
						<div class="comment-text w-full" itemprop="text"><p>I see several others asking about dairy-free options for this, so I wanted to add my experience since I have made this sauce 3 times now, about to make it for a 4th for my meal-prep to finish out this New Year’s week!</p>
<p>I make this sauce with Earth Balance vegan butter sticks and full fat canned coconut milk in place of the cream.  The sauce does not come out quite as thick as it would with dairy cream, but it is still extremely flavorful and does still thicken up a bit.  I tried using cornstarch once to add to the thickness, but this ended up separating later on, I assume by contribution of the acidity from the lemon, so definitely won’t be trying that trick again.  Just sticking with the cocomilk.</p>
<p>I like to make my salmon with crispy potatoes and green beans and I just smother all of it in the sauce because it pairs so well with everything on the plate.   Shallots are SO underrated and I’m keen to have a recipe I’ll make so often which uses one.  In full disclosure: I only use this recipe for the sauce since I’ve got my own tried-and-true method for crispy potats, but this sauce will absolutely remain part of my meal-prep rotation for the foreseeable future.</p>
<p>Many thanks for this one, Krista!</p>
